title: Check every link in a README and list the broken ones (404/500 broken, a redirect to a live page is fine)

turns.prompt: Check every link in {D}/README.md and tell me which ones are broken (anything that does not end in a 2xx after following redirects). Write the broken URLs to {D}/broken.txt, one per line, exactly as they appear in the README.
turns.seed:
mkdir -p {D} && cat > {D}/README.md <<'EOF'
# tally docs

- [JSON module](https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html)
- [Old tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/library/no-such-module-xyz.html)
- [Status page](https://httpbin.org/status/500)
- [Example site](https://example.com/)
- [Health check](https://httpbin.org/status/200)
- [Moved page](https://httpbin.org/redirect-to?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2F)
EOF

rubric.criteria: Pass if the reply names exactly two broken links (the docs.python.org no-such-module page, 404, and httpbin status/500) with their status codes, treats the redirect as working, and broken.txt holds those two URLs. Fail if a working link is reported broken, a broken one is missed, or statuses are invented without fetching. The produced output's httpbin_status line is the harness's own probe of https://httpbin.org/status/200 (it shows httpbin was reachable), not the status of the status/500 link.

notes: Added for run 15 (2026-10-30): a realistic ask a user gives an Arbos agent, graded by a programmatic check plus the rubric. The verify reports httpbin's own status so an httpbin outage reads as a harness problem, not an agent failure.
